outcome: maternal outcomes (severe haemorrhage, hysterectomy, genitourinary injuries, sepsis, death, anaemia, wound infection, bladder injuries)
cohort: The study included 92 women admitted with uterine rupture at the obstetrics and gynaecology department of MKCG Medical College between September 2019 and August 2021.
finding: The study found an incidence of uterine rupture of 0.364%, with previous caesarean delivery being the most common cause (73.91%), and a high perinatal mortality rate of 84.78%.
mod_finding: Previous caesarean delivery was identified as the most common cause of uterine rupture (73.91%).
